TITLE: UAE investigates source of drones after 'treacherous terrorist attack' on Barakah plant
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-17 (updated 2026-05-18 00:42)
SOURCE: The National (UAE)

KEY FACTS:
- 3 drones entered UAE from western border on Sunday
- 2 intercepted by air defence systems
- 1 caused fire at electrical generator outside inner perimeter of Barakah Nuclear Power Plant
- No injuries; no radiological release
- IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi: "Military activity that threatens nuclear safety is unacceptable" — calls for "maximum military restraint" near nuclear plants
- Emergency diesel generators providing power to Unit 3
- Officials have not attributed responsibility; "western border" reference rather than Iran in east
- Not clear if Iranian allies (Houthis, Iraqi militias) mounted the strike

SHEIKH ABDULLAH bin Zayed (Deputy PM + Foreign Minister) condemnation:
- "Treacherous terrorist attack"
- Strike represented breach of international law (in phone call with IAEA Grossi)
- UAE has "full right to respond to these terrorist attacks and to take all necessary measures to protect its security, territorial integrity, and citizens, in accordance with international law"

MoFA statement:
- Attack constitutes "dangerous escalation"
- "Unacceptable act of aggression" and "direct threat to the country's security"
- Targeting peaceful nuclear energy facilities a "flagrant violation of international law, the UN charter, and the principles of humanitarian law"
- UAE "would not tolerate any threat to its security and reserved its right to respond"

CONTEXT:
- UAE notably did NOT name Iran (previous attacks have done so)
- Emirates and Gulf states have faced "barrage of missile and drone strikes" launched by Iran since war broke out Feb 28
- Conditional ceasefire US/Iran agreed Apr 8 led to halt for several weeks
- Tehran resumed strikes on Emirates earlier this month
- MoD: armed forces remained ready to confront threats, would respond firmly
